   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationsPolicy" id="c142189002" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Business Combinations and Asset Acquisitions</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The Company&#160;evaluates each acquisition transaction to determine whether the acquired asset meets the definition of a business and therefore should be accounted for as a business combination, or if the transaction should be accounted for as an asset acquisition. Under&#160;ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">805,</em> <i>Business Combinations</i>, an acquisition does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> qualify as a business when substantially all of the fair value is concentrated in a single identifiable asset or group of similar identifiable&#160;assets. If the Company determines that the screen test is met, the transaction is accounted for as an asset acquisition. If the screen test is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> met, the Company further considers whether&#160;the acquisition includes, at a minimum, inputs and processes that have the ability to create outputs in the form of revenue. If the assets acquired meet this criteria, the transaction is accounted for as a business combination.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The Company accounts for acquisitions that qualify as asset acquisitions utilizing a cost accumulation model whereby the purchase price of the acquisition is allocated to the assets acquired on a relative fair value basis on the date of acquisition. Inputs used to determine such fair values are primarily based upon internally developed models, publicly-available&#160; information, a risk-adjusted discount rate and/or publicly-available data regarding transactions consummated by other market participants, as applicable.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The Company&#160;accounts for business combinations&#160;using the acquisition method of accounting under ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">805,</em> <i>Business Combinations</i>, whereby the total purchase price is allocated to tangible and intangible assets acquired and liabilities assumed based on respective estimated fair values. The initial valuations are derived from estimated fair value assessments and assumptions used by managements. The excess of the acquisition price over those estimated fair values, if any, is recorded as goodwill.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">Transaction-related costs related to asset acquisitions are capitalized as part of the cost basis of the acquired assets. Transaction-related expenses and restructuring costs that are deemed to be part of an acquisition of a business are expensed as incurred.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:RevenueRecognitionPolicyTextBlock" id="c142189003" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Revenue recognition </i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The Company leases the hangar facilities that it constructs to&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">third</em>&#160;parties.&#160;The Company determines whether a contract contains a lease at the inception of the contract. The lease agreements are either on a month-to-month basis or have a defined term and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>have options to extend the term. Some of the leases contain options to terminate the lease by either party with given notice. The Company expects to continue to derive benefit from the underlying assets after the end of the lease term through further leasing arrangements. The underlying assets are the leasehold interest that the Company has in connection with its ground leases. There are&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;options given to the lessee to purchase the underlying assets.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">Rental revenue is recognized in accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">842</em> and includes fixed payments of cash rents, which represents revenue each tenant pays in accordance with the terms of its respective lease and is recognized on a straight-line basis over the term of the lease. Rental revenue and the corresponding rent and other receivables are recorded net of any concessions and uncollectible tenant receivables for all periods presented. The Company evaluates the collectability of tenant receivables for payments required under the lease agreements. If the Company determines that collectability is&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;probable, the Company recognizes any difference between revenue amounts recognized to date under ASC&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">842</em>&#160;and payments that have been collected from the lessee, including any additional rent or lease termination fees, as a current period adjustment to rental revenue.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">At certain of the Company's hangar campuses, the Company recognizes revenue from ground-based services, such as the fueling and towing of aircraft. Revenue for the sale of&#160;aircraft fuel&#160;is recognized at the time customer obtains control of the fuel. Revenue for the sale of other ground-based services is recognized at the time&#160;the service is performed and provided to customers. Customers are invoiced at the time the services are performed and the associated revenue is recognized in the period it is earned. The Company's fueling arrangements generally are unique at each location it operates, and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be accounted for on a gross or net basis. The Company determines whether to recognize fuel and services revenue on a gross or net basis based on consideration of various factors, including whether the Company has control of the products or services prior to delivery to customers, the Company's degree of latitude in establishing the sales price, whether the Company carries the associated inventory risk, and which party is the primary obligor within such sales arrangements.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">For the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, the Company did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> derive <em style="font: inherit;">10%</em> or more of its revenue from any single tenant.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:AdvertisingCostsPolicyTextBlock" id="c142189004" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Advertising Costs</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company expenses the cost of advertising and marketing as incurred. Advertising and marketing costs recognized as&#160;pursuit and marketing expenses totaled approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188298" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AdvertisingExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>,&#160;and approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188300" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AdvertisingExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.4</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c142189005" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Income Taxes</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">SHG is classified as a corporation for Federal income tax purposes and is subject to U.S. Federal and state income taxes. SHG includes in income, for U.S. Federal income tax purposes, its allocable portion of income from the &#8220;pass-through&#8221; entities in which it holds an interest, including Sky. The &#8220;pass-through&#8221; entities, are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subject to U.S. Federal and certain state income taxes at the entity level, and instead, the tax liabilities with respect to taxable income are passed through to the members, including SHG. As a result, prior to the Yellowstone Transaction, Sky was <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subject to U.S. Federal and certain state income taxes at the entity level.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company follows the asset and liability method of accounting for income taxes. This method gives consideration to the future tax consequences associated with the differences between the financial accounting and tax basis of the assets and liabilities as well as the ultimate realization of any deferred tax asset resulting from such differences, as well as from net operating losses and other tax-basis carryforwards. Valuation allowances are recorded to reduce deferred tax assets when it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that a tax benefit will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be realized. When a valuation allowance is increased or decreased, a corresponding tax expense or benefit is recorded.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Amounts payable under the Tax Receivable Agreement, as defined in Note <em style="font: inherit;">14</em>&#160;<i>&#8212; Income Taxes</i>, are accrued by a charge to income when it is probable that a liability has been incurred and the amount is estimable.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c142189006" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 0pt;"><b><i>Recently Adopted Accounting Pronouncements</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i>Income Taxes (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">740</em>)</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09,</em> <i>Income Taxes (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">740</em>): Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures</i>. The amendments in this update applied to all entities that are subject to Topic <em style="font: inherit;">740,</em><i> Income Taxes</i>. The standard requires&#160;disaggregated information about a reporting entity's effective tax rate reconciliation as well as information on income taxes paid. The amendments in this update are effective for annual periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2024. </em>The guidance will be applied on a prospective basis with the option to apply the standard retrospectively. The Company adopted ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em> effective <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 0pt;"><b><i>Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i>Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses&#160;(Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">220</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>)</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em> <i>Income Statement&#160;&#8212; Reporting Comprehensive Income: Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">220</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses</i>. This ASU requires public business entities to disclose in the notes to financial statements specific categories within relevant expense captions presented on the face of the income statement. The ASU is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027. </em>Early adoption is permitted. The amendments should be applied on a prospective basis with retrospective application permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of adopting this ASU on our consolidated financial statements and disclosures.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i>Interim Reporting Requirements (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">270</em>)</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025, </em>the FASB issued&#160;ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">11,</em>&#160;<i>Interim Reporting (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">270</em>): Narrow-Scope Improvements</i>. This ASU&#160;intends to improve the navigability of the guidance in ASC <em style="font: inherit;">270,</em>&#160;Interim Reporting&#160;(&#8220;ASC <em style="font: inherit;">270&#8221;</em>), and clarifies when it applies. The&#160;ASU&#160;also provides additional guidance on what disclosures should be provided in interim reporting periods and establishes a principle under which an entity must disclose events since the end of the last annual reporting period that have had material impact on the entity. The guidance is effective for annual periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027, </em>including interim periods within those fiscal years. Early adoption is permitted and entities <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>apply the guidance prospectively or retrospectively. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of adopting this ASU on our consolidated financial statements and disclosures.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> December 6, 2024&#160;(</em>the &#8220;CMA Closing Date&#8221;), the Company,&#160;through <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> wholly-owned subsidiaries of&#160; Sky, completed the acquisition of CloudNine at Camarillo LP (&#8220;CloudNine&#8221;), a California limited partnership, and Sky <em style="font: inherit;">805</em> LLC (&#8220;Sky <em style="font: inherit;">805&#8221;</em>), California limited liability company in exchange for approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188335" contextRef="d_2024-12-06_2024-12-06_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-CamarilloAcquisitionMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred1" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">32.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in aggregate cash consideration (collectively, the &#8220;Camarillo Acquisitions&#8221;).    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The Company&#8217;s long-term ground leases have remaining terms ranging between <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_LeaseContractualTermAxis-GroundLeasesAtSgrOpfAndBnaMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" id="c142188383" format="ixt-sec:duryear">18</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_LeaseContractualTermAxis-GroundLeasesAtSgrOpfAndBnaMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" id="c142188384" format="ixt-sec:duryear">71</ix:nonNumeric> years, including options for the Company to extend the terms. Certain of the Company's ground leases contain options to lease additional parcels of land at the Company's option within a specified period of time.&#160;In addition to the Company&#8217;s ground leases, the Company has operating leases for office space and ground support vehicles,&#160;and finance leases for vehicles supporting operations at our pre-engineered metal building subsidiary.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> March 2024,&#160;</em>the Company, through an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, entered into a ground lease agreement (the &#8220;SJC Lease&#8221;) at SJC&#160;with the City of San Jose.    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> March 2024,&#160;</em>the Company, through an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, entered into a ground lease agreement&#160;(the &#8220;ORL Lease&#8221;) at ORL with the Greater Orlando Aviation Authority (&#8220;GOAA&#8221;). The ORL Lease covers a parcel containing approximately&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142188394" contextRef="i_2024-03-27_LeaseContractualTermAxis-ORLLeaseMember" unitRef="Acre" name="us-gaap:AreaOfLand" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">20</ix:nonFraction>&#160;acres of land at ORL. The initial term of the ORL Lease will be&#160;<ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2024-03-27_LeaseContractualTermAxis-ORLLeaseMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" id="c142188395" format="ixt-sec:duryear">30</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;years from expiration of construction period, with lease payments commencing contemporaneously with the term. The ORL Lease contains options exercisable by the Company to extend the ORL Lease an additional&#160;<ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2024-03-27_LeaseContractualTermAxis-ORLLeaseMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRenewalTerm" id="c142188396" format="ixt-sec:duryear">20</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;years based on the Company's total expenditures in subsequent phases at ORL.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> May 2024, </em>the Company, through an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, entered into a ground lease agreement (the &#8220;IAD&#160;Lease&#8221;) at IAD with the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority (&#8220;MWAA&#8221;). The IAD Lease covers approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c142188397" contextRef="i_2024-05-31_LeaseContractualTermAxis-IadLeaseMember" unitRef="Acre" name="us-gaap:AreaOfLand" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">18</ix:nonFraction>&#160;acres of property at IAD. The initial term of the IAD Lease will be approximately <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2024-05-31_LeaseContractualTermAxis-IadLeaseMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" id="c142188398" format="ixt-sec:duryear">50</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;years and expire on <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2074, </em>and contains an option exercisable by the Company to extend the IAD Lease&#160;an additional <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2024-05-31_LeaseContractualTermAxis-IadLeaseMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRenewalTerm" id="c142188399" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> years following the expiration of the initial term. The property covered by the IAD Lease is split between <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> parcels, with rent payments associated with the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> parcel (&#8220;IAD&#160;Phase I&#8221;) commencing the earlier of certificate of occupancy or <em style="font: inherit;">36</em> months from the issuance of permits for IAD Phase I, and rent payments associated with the <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> parcel (&#8220;IAD&#160;Phase II&#8221;) commencing the earlier of issuance of permits for IAD Phase II or <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> years from certificate of occupancy associated with IAD Phase I.&#160;The IAD&#160;Lease requires the Company to commence construction related to IAD Phase II within <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> years of the receipt of the certificate of occupancy for IAD Phase I.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> August 2024, </em>the Company, through an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, entered into a ground lease agreement (the &#8220;SLC Lease&#8221;) at Salt Lake City International Airport (&#8220;SLC&#8221;)&#160;with the Salt Lake City Corporation. The SLC Lease covers approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c142188406" contextRef="i_2024-08-31_LeaseContractualTermAxis-SlcLeaseMember" unitRef="Acre" name="us-gaap:AreaOfLand" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">8.4</ix:nonFraction> acres of property at SLC.    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 9pt; text-align: justify;">The amounts presented above exclude tenant variable payments, rental escalations that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> fixed, or future rental revenue from the renewal or replacement of existing tenant leases.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">Variable payments consist of recoveries from tenants&#160;for common area maintenance, utilities, and operating expenses of the property, and various other fees, including fees associated with the delivery of aircraft fuel, late fees, short-term rentals, and lease termination fees. Variable payments are charged based on the terms and conditions included in the respective tenant leases and are recognized in the same period as the expenses are incurred.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Bonds payable</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 20, 2021, </em>Sky formed a new wholly-owned subsidiary, Sky Harbour Capital LLC, as a parent corporation to its wholly-owned subsidiaries that operate each of the aircraft hangar development sites under its <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> <em style="font: inherit;">six</em> ground leases. Sky Harbour Capital LLC and these subsidiaries form an Obligated Group (the &#8220;Obligated Group&#8221; or the &#8220;Borrowers&#8221;) under a series of bonds that were issued in <em style="font: inherit;"> September 2021 </em>with a principal amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188445" contextRef="i_2021-05-20_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-Series2021BondsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentCarryingAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">166.3</ix:nonFraction> million (the &#8220;Series <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Bonds&#8221;). The members of the Obligated Group are jointly and severally liable under the Series <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Bonds. SHG and its other subsidiaries are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> members of the Obligated Group and have <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> obligation to repay the bonds.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Series <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Bonds are payable pursuant to a loan agreement dated <em style="font: inherit;"> September 1, 2021 </em>between the Public Finance Authority (of Wisconsin) and the Borrowers. The payments by the Borrowers under the loan agreement are secured by a Senior Master Indenture Promissory Note, Series <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">1</em> issued by the Obligated Group under an indenture (the &#8220;Master Indenture&#8221;). The obligations of the Borrowers are collateralized by certain leasehold and sub-leasehold deeds of trust or mortgages on the Borrowers&#8217; interests in the development sites and facilities being constructed at each airport where the Borrowers hold ground leases. In addition, the Borrowers have assigned, pledged and granted a <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> priority security interest in all funds held under the Master Indenture and all right, title and interest in the gross revenues of the Borrowers. Furthermore, Sky, Sky Harbour Holdings LLC and Sky Harbour Capital LLC have each pledged as collateral its respective ownership interest in any of the Borrowers.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Series <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Bonds have principal amounts, interest rates, and maturity dates as follow: $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188455" contextRef="i_2021-05-20_DebtInstrumentAxis-TrancheOneMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-Series2021BondsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentCarryingAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">21.1</ix:nonFraction> million bearing interest at <ix:nonFraction id="c142188456" contextRef="i_2021-05-20_DebtInstrumentAxis-TrancheOneMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-Series2021BondsMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">4.00</ix:nonFraction>%, due <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2036; </em>$<ix:nonFraction id="c142188457" contextRef="i_2021-05-20_DebtInstrumentAxis-TrancheTwoMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-Series2021BondsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentCarryingAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">30.4</ix:nonFraction> million bearing interest at <ix:nonFraction id="c142188458" contextRef="i_2021-05-20_DebtInstrumentAxis-TrancheTwoMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-Series2021BondsMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">4.00</ix:nonFraction>%, due <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2041; </em>and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188459" contextRef="i_2021-05-20_DebtInstrumentAxis-TrancheThreeMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-Series2021BondsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentCarryingAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">114.8</ix:nonFraction> million bearing interest at <ix:nonFraction id="c142188460" contextRef="i_2021-05-20_DebtInstrumentAxis-TrancheThreeMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-Series2021BondsMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">4.25</ix:nonFraction>%, due <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2054. </em>The Series <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Bond that has a maturity date of <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2036 </em>was issued at a premium, and the Company received bond proceeds that were $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188462" contextRef="i_2021-05-20_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-Series2021BondsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentUnamortizedPremium" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.2</ix:nonFraction> million above its face value. The bond premium is being amortized as a reduction of interest expense over the life of the bond. Interest is payable on each <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, </em>commencing <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2022. </em>Principal repayments due under the Series <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Bonds are paid annually, commencing <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2032.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company was in compliance with all&#160;debt covenants&#160;as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">31,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025.</em> As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, </em>the fair value of the Company's Series <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Bonds was approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188467" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis-FairValueInputsLevel2Member_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-Series2021BondsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">140.8</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188468" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_FairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis-FairValueInputsLevel2Member_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-Series2021BondsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">143.8</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively. The fair value of the Company's bonds is estimated utilizing Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> inputs including prices for the bonds on inactive markets.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 9pt;"><i>Tax-Exempt Warehouse Facility</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 4, 2025,&#160;</em>Sky Harbour Capital II LLC (&#8220;SH Capital II&#8221;), an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, entered into a Draw Down Note Purchase And Continuing Covenant Agreement (the &#8220;Credit Agreement&#8221;), among SH Capital II, the other borrowers party thereto, the lenders party thereto (the &#8220;Lenders&#8221;) and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., as administrative agent, sole bookrunner and sole lead arranger (&#8220;JPMorgan&#8221; or &#8220;Administrative Agent&#8221;). The Credit Agreement provides for, among other things, a term loan facility in an aggregate principal amount of up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188473" contextRef="i_2025-09-04_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">200</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million (the &#8220;Term Loan Facility&#8221;) at any&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">one</em>&#160;time outstanding. The Term Loan Facility provides for borrowings under the Credit Agreement (the &#8220;Loans&#8221;) to be made by the Lenders from time to time as requested by SH Capital II. The Lenders will make funds available to the Term Loan Borrowers (as defined below) through the purchase of notes issued by the Issuer (as defined below) pursuant to the Loan and Security Agreement (as defined below) so that the Issuer&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>fund the Loans to Borrowers. The Loans will mature on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 4, 2030,&#160;</em>subject to any extensions by the Lenders. The Term Loan Facility&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>be increased, subject to credit approval, up to an aggregate principal amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188475" contextRef="i_2025-09-04_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="skyh:DebtInstrumentFaceAmountPossible" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">300</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">The Credit Agreement provides for Loans to be made from time to time by special purpose subsidiaries of SH Capital II (SH Capital II together with the special purpose subsidiaries, the &#8220;Term Loan Borrowers&#8221;) for the construction and operation of hangar project facilities at various airports (the &#8220;Hangar Projects&#8221;), subject to customary phased eligibility criteria. Loans will be secured by the real estate underlying the Hangar Projects, pledges of equity interests in the Term Loan Borrowers and certain revenues of the Term Loan Borrowers. Sky Harbour LLC, the Company&#8217;s operating company, and Sky Harbour Holdings II LLC, the holding company of SH Capital II, and Sky Harbour Holdings III LLC (&#8220;SKYH III&#8221;) will guarantee the Term Loan Borrowers&#8217; obligations under the Loans pursuant to a Parent Guarantee and a Holdco Guaranty, respectively.&#160;In addition, pursuant to a Non-Recourse Carveout Guaranty, the Company will be required to guarantee the Term Loan Borrowers&#8217; obligations under the Loans in certain limited circumstances such as misconduct by the Term Loan Borrowers or the primary guarantors. In addition, SKYH III has entered into a Pledge and Security Agreement with the Administrative Agent pursuant to which it will pledge its interest in an account ( the &#8220;Facility Cash Flow Account&#8221;) into which will be deposited amounts received by Sky Harbour LLC from excess revenues released from the Master Trust Indenture (Security Agreement), dated as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> August 1, 2021,&#160;</em>among Sky Harbour Capital LLC, the Obligated Group, and The Bank of New York Mellon, as master trustee, as amended from time to time and as joined from time to time by additional members as permitted therein (the &#8220;Term Loan Master Indenture&#8221;).&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">No</em>&#160;excess revenues are permitted to be released from the Term Loan Master Indenture until, among other things, substantial completion of the projects financed by the Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2021</em>&#160;Bonds for the benefit of Obligated Group (the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2021</em>&#160;Projects&#8221;).</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Certain events&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>disqualify a Hangar Project from further Loans and trigger prepayments such as the cancellation or termination of a construction contract or a ground lease or a material violation of environmental law. The Credit Agreement also has customary and other mandatory prepayment events including the obligation to prepay amounts to bring Company back into compliance with the Leverage Ratio (as defined below).</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Loans under the Credit Agreement will bear interest at a rate of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142188479" contextRef="d_2025-09-04_2025-09-04_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="skyh:DebtInstrumentInterestRatePercentageOfSumOfSofrAnd01" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">80</ix:nonFraction>% of the sum of&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142188926">SOFR</span>&#160;and&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142188480" contextRef="d_2025-09-04_2025-09-04_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="skyh:DebtInstrumentDefaultRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">0.10</ix:nonFraction>%, plus&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142188481" contextRef="d_2025-09-04_2025-09-04_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">200</ix:nonFraction>&#160;basis points. Interest payments&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>be capitalized, at the option of the Term Loan Borrowers, during the earlier of (i) the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">first</em>&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;years of the Term Loan Facility or (ii) the substantial completion of the hangar projects contemplated by the Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2021</em>&#160;Bonds. The entire principal amount of the Loans is due on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 4, 2030,&#160;</em>unless extended in accordance with the Credit Agreement. Once the outstanding aggregate principal balance of the Loans reaches $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188485" contextRef="i_2025-09-04_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="skyh:DebtInstrumentLoanOutstandingBenchmark" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">25</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, the Term Loan Borrowers are obligated, to have hedges on&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142188486" contextRef="d_2025-09-04_2025-09-04_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="skyh:DebtInstrumentInterestRateRiskHedge" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">50</ix:nonFraction>% of the Term Loan Borrowers&#8217; interest rate risk.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">In accordance with the Credit Agreement, the Term Loan Borrowers have paid an upfront fee equal to&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142188487" contextRef="d_2025-09-04_2025-09-04_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="skyh:DebtInstrumentUpfrontFee" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">1.50</ix:nonFraction>% of the $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188488" contextRef="i_2025-09-04_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">200</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in Loans commitments. The Credit Agreement also requires the Term Loan Borrowers to pay quarterly&#160;commitment fees to the Administrative Agent for the benefit of the secured lenders at the applicable rate per annum set forth below under the caption &#8220;Commitment Fee Rate,&#8221; based upon the Term Loan Borrowers&#8217; total commitment utilization in effect for each such day during each quarter:</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">The Credit Agreement contains customary affirmative and negative covenants for transactions of this type, including&#160;maintenance of financial ratios, debt service reserve requirements, restricted payments test and limitations on the sale, lease, or distribution of assets. The Term Loan Borrowers agreed to comply with historical and projected debt service coverage ratios. The Projected Debt Service Coverage Ratio (the &#8220;Projected DSCR&#8221;) is based principally on projected EBITDA of Hangar Projects that have reached substantial completion (&#8220;Hangar Project EBITDA&#8221;) minus certain capital expenditure and taxes divided by the debt service for the next&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">four</em>&#160;quarters. The Historical Debt Service Coverage Ratio (the &#8220;Historical DSCR&#8221;) is based on the Hangar Project EBITDA for the previous&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">four</em>&#160;quarters minus the sum of certain capital expenditures plus taxes divided by the interest of debt service for the previous&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">four</em>&#160;quarters. For this purpose, &#8220;EBITDA&#8221; is defined to include amounts in the Facility Surplus Account. Additionally, the Term Loan Borrowers agreed to a Leverage Ratio of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142188492" contextRef="d_2025-09-04_2025-09-04_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="skyh:LeverageRatio" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">65</ix:nonFraction>% (the &#8220;Leverage Ratio&#8221;). The Leverage Ratio is calculated by dividing total indebtedness of the Term Loan Borrowers by a borrowing base value. The borrowing base value is principally the sum of project costs for the Hangar Projects or, in the case that an existing Hangar Project is used as collateral, net purchase price plus certain reserves established pursuant to the Credit Agreement and financed transaction costs. Commencing&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;months after the earlier of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 4, 2028&#160;</em>or a trigger date based on substantial completion of certain Hangar Projects, the Term Loan Borrowers are required to maintain (i) the Historical DSCR, or (ii) the Projected DSCR, in each case determined on the last day of each fiscal quarter of the Term Loan Borrowers, at a ratio of less than&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142188494" contextRef="d_2025-09-04_2025-09-04_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="skyh:DscrRatio" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1.25</ix:nonFraction>&#160;to&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">1.00.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">In connection with the Credit Agreement, SH Capital II entered into a Loan and Security Agreement (the &#8220;Loan and Security Agreement&#8221;), with Public Finance Authority (of Wisconsin)&#160;(the &#8220;Issuer&#8221;), SH Capital II, the other borrowers party thereto, and the Administrative Agent. The Loan and Security Agreement provides for, among other things, the issuance of up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188496" contextRef="i_2025-09-04_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">200</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of Sky Harbour Obligated Group II Issue, Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Notes (the &#8220;Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Notes&#8221;). If the Lenders under the Credit Agreement approve an increase in the Term Loan Facility, additional Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Notes will be issued. The Loan and Security Agreement and the Series&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Notes further provide for the Issuer to assign all revenues on the Notes to the Administrative Agent for the benefit of the secured lenders and provide for the incorporation of certain covenants from the Credit Agreement and customary terms and conditions for financings of this type.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> October 2025,&#160;</em>the Company entered into an interest rate swap (the &#8220;Swap Agreement&#8221;) for&#160;notional amounts of up to&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142188501" contextRef="i_2025-10-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-InterestRateSwapMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">200</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, based on predetermined notional schedule agreement as defined in the Swap Agreement. The Swap Agreement&#160;effectively fixes the SOFR component of any loans at or below the notional schedule made&#160;under the Term Loan Facility at&#160;approximately&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142188502" contextRef="i_2025-10-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-InterestRateSwapMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DerivativeVariableInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">2.65</ix:nonFraction>%, or&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142188503" contextRef="i_2025-10-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-InterestRateSwapMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DerivativeVariableInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">4.73</ix:nonFraction>% inclusive of applicable interest rate spreads, for the&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142188504">five</span>-year term. Beginning on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 1, 2027, </em>the <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> Vista Loan will bear fixed interest at a rate of the greater&#160;of (i) the sum of the <em style="font: inherit;">30</em>-day term SOFR rate and <ix:nonFraction id="c142188532" contextRef="d_2027-02-01_2027-02-01_DebtInstrumentAxis-VistaLoan2025Member_StatementScenarioAxis-ScenarioForecastMember_VariableRateAxis-SecuredOvernightFinancingRateSofrMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">2.25</ix:nonFraction>% or (ii) <ix:nonFraction id="c142188533" contextRef="i_2027-02-01_DebtInstrumentAxis-VistaLoan2025Member_RangeAxis-MinimumMember_StatementScenarioAxis-ScenarioForecastMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">5.0</ix:nonFraction>%.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">SHG's legal predecessor, Yellowstone Acquisition Company (&#8220;YAC&#8221;) issued to <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party investors <ix:nonFraction id="c142188540" contextRef="i_2020-10-26_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PublicWarrantsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightNumberOfSecuritiesCalledByWarrantsOrRights" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">6,799,439</ix:nonFraction> warrants which entitled the holder to purchase <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> share of Class A Common Stock at an exercise price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188542" contextRef="i_2020-10-26_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PublicWarrantsMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">11.50</ix:nonFraction> per share (the &#8220;Public Warrants&#8221;). In addition, <ix:nonFraction id="c142188543" contextRef="i_2020-10-26_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PrivatePlacementWarrantMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightNumberOfSecuritiesCalledByWarrantsOrRights" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">7,719,779</ix:nonFraction> private placement warrants were sold to the Sponsor. Each Private Warrant allows the Sponsor to purchase <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> share of Class A Common Stock at an exercise price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188545" contextRef="i_2020-10-26_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PrivatePlacementWarrantMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">11.50</ix:nonFraction> per share. The Public Warrants and Private Warrants remain outstanding under the same terms and conditions to purchase shares of the Company&#8217;s Class A Common Stock. The terms of the Private Warrants are identical to those of the Public Warrants, except for that so long as the Private Warrants are held by the Sponsor or its permitted transferees, they <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be exercised on a cashless basis.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">In connection with the&#160;Securities Purchase Agreement (the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2023</em>&#160;Purchase Agreement&#8221;) entered into on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 1, 2023&#160;</em>with certain investors, the Company issued to&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party investors&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142188548" contextRef="i_2023-11-01_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PrivatePlacementWarrantMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightNumberOfSecuritiesCalledByWarrantsOrRights" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,541,600</ix:nonFraction>&#160;warrants (the &#8220;PIPE Warrants&#8221;, and together with the Public Warrants and the Private Warrants, the &#8220;Warrants&#8221;). The PIPE Warrants are equivalent in form and substance to the Company&#8217;s Public Warrants.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The Warrants contain an exercise price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188549" contextRef="i_2023-11-01_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PrivatePlacementWarrantMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">11.50</ix:nonFraction> per share and expire on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 25, 2027. </em>The Company determined the fair value of its Public Warrants and PIPE Warrants based on the publicly listed trading price as of the valuation date. Accordingly, these warrants are classified as Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> financial instruments. As the terms of the Private Warrants are identical to those of the Public Warrants, the Company determined the fair value of its Private Warrants based on the publicly listed trading price of the Public Warrants as of the valuation date and have classified the Private Warrants as Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> financial instruments.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><ix:nonFraction id="c142188552" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PrivatePlacementWarrantMember" unitRef="Share" name="skyh:ClassOfWarrantsOrRightsExercisedDuringPeriod" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">No</ix:nonFraction> Warrants were exercised during the year&#160;ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025. </em>During the year&#160;ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, </em><ix:nonFraction id="c142188553" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PrivatePlacementWarrantMember" unitRef="Share" name="skyh:ClassOfWarrantsOrRightsExercisedDuringPeriod" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">262,188</ix:nonFraction> Warrants were exercised, resulting in approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188554" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PrivatePlacementWarrantMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromWarrantExercises" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">3.0</ix:nonFraction> million of proceeds. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, <ix:nonFraction id="c142188556" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PrivatePlacementWarrantMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightOutstanding" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">15,798,155</ix:nonFraction> Warrants remain outstanding.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The closing price of the Warrants was $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188557" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PrivatePlacementWarrantMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="skyh:ClassOfWarrantsAndRightsOutsandingPrice" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.65</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188558" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-PrivatePlacementWarrantMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="skyh:ClassOfWarrantsAndRightsOutsandingPrice" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2.92</ix:nonFraction> per warrant on <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, </em>respectively.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Common Equity</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, there were <ix:nonFraction id="c142188568" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-CommonClassAMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">33,989,673</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction id="c142188569" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_StatementClassOfStockAxis-CommonClassBMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">42,046,356</ix:nonFraction> shares of Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock outstanding, respectively. Holders of Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock vote together as a single class on all matters submitted to the stockholders for their vote or approval, except as required by applicable law. Holders of Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock are entitled to <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> vote per share on all matters submitted to the stockholders for their vote or approval.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The holders of Class A Common Stock are entitled to receive dividends, as and if declared by the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors out of legally available funds. With respect to stock dividends, holders of Class A Common Stock must receive Class A Common Stock. The holders of Class B Common Stock do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have any right to receive dividends other than stock dividends consisting of shares of Class B Common Stock, as applicable, in each case paid proportionally with respect to each outstanding share of Class B Common Stock.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 9pt;"><i>At-the-Market Facility</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> March 27, 2024, </em>the Company entered into an At Market Issuance Sales Agreement (the &#8220;ATM Agreement&#8221;) with&#160;B. Riley&#160;Securities, Inc. (&#8220;B. Riley&#8221;) with respect to an &#8220;at the market&#8221; offering program (the &#8220;ATM Facility&#8221;), under which the Company&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may, </em>from time to time, at its sole discretion, issue and sell through&#160;B. Riley, acting as sales agent, up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188572" contextRef="i_2024-03-27_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtMarketIssuanceSalesAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="skyh:SaleOfStockMaximumAmountIssuable" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">100</ix:nonFraction> million of shares of&#160;Class A Common Stock. Pursuant to the ATM Agreement, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>sell the shares through&#160;B. Riley by any method permitted that is deemed an &#8220;at the market&#8221; offering as defined in Rule <em style="font: inherit;">415</em> under the Securities Act.&#160;B. Riley will use commercially reasonable efforts consistent with its normal trading and sales practices to sell the shares from time to time, based upon instructions from the Company, including any price or size limits or other customary parameters or conditions the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>impose. The Company&#160;will pay&#160;B. Riley&#160;a commission of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142188574" contextRef="i_2024-03-27_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtMarketIssuanceSalesAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="skyh:SaleOfStockCommissionPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">3.0</ix:nonFraction>% of the gross sales price per share sold under the ATM Agreement, subject to certain reductions.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> obligated to sell any shares under the ATM Agreement. The offering of shares pursuant to the ATM Agreement will terminate upon the earlier to occur of (i) the issuance and sale, through&#160;B. Riley, of all of the shares subject to the ATM Agreement and (ii) termination of the ATM Agreement in accordance with its terms.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">In connection with entering into the ATM Agreement, on <em style="font: inherit;"> March 27, 2024, </em>the Company and B. Riley terminated (the &#8220;B. Riley Termination&#8221;) the Common Stock Purchase Agreement (the &#8220;B. Riley Stock Purchase Agreement&#8221;) dated <em style="font: inherit;"> August 18, 2022. </em>As a result of the B. Riley Termination, the Company recognized approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188576" contextRef="d_2024-03-27_2024-03-27_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-AtMarketIssuanceSalesAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsOfStockIssuanceCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction> million of expense associated with the write-off of deferred equity issuance costs. From <em style="font: inherit;"> August 18, 2022 </em>through <em style="font: inherit;"> March 27, 2024, </em>the Company had <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> directed B. Riley to purchase any Class A Common Stock pursuant to the B. Riley Stock Purchase Agreement.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Non-controlling interests</i></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The LLC Interests&#8217; ownership in Sky is presented as non-controlling interests within the Equity section of the consolidated balance sheet as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> and represents the Sky Common Units held by holders other than SHG. The holders of LLC Interests <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>exchange Sky Common Units along with an equal number of Class B Common Shares, for Class A Common Shares on the Company. The LLC Interests do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have the option to redeem their Sky Common Units for cash or a variable number of Class A Common Shares, nor does SHG have the option to settle a redemption in such a manner. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, the LLC interests owned approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c142188654" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_LegalEntityAxis-LLCInterestsAndTRAHoldersMember_OwnershipAxis-SkyHarbourLLCMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:MinorityInterestOwnershipPercentageByNoncontrollingOwners" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">55.3</ix:nonFraction>% of the Sky Common Units outstanding.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The former majority shareholder's ownership in Overflow was presented as a non-controlling interest within the Equity section of the consolidated balance sheet. On <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, </em>the Company assumed the former majority shareholder's ownership interest in Overflow for <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> consideration.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> January 25, 2022, </em>the Company's&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Incentive Award Plan (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2022</em> Incentive Award Plan&#8221;) became effective following approval by the Company's shareholders. The <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Incentive Award Plan provides for grants of stock-based compensation awards, including without limitation, non-qualified stock options, incentive stock options, stock appreciation rights, or SARs, restricted stock awards, restricted stock unit awards, incentive unit awards other stock or cash based awards and dividend equivalent awards. Employees, officers, and consultants of the Company or any parent or affiliate, including Sky, or any non-employee director of the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors are eligible to receive awards under the <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Incentive Award Plan. An aggregate of approximately <ix:nonFraction id="c142188662" contextRef="i_2022-01-25_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_GranteeStatusAxis-ShareBasedPaymentArrangementEmployeeMember_PlanNameAxis-The2022IncentiveAwardPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">6.2</ix:nonFraction> million shares of Class A Common Stock are issuable pursuant to the <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Incentive Award Plan.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 9pt;"><i>Non-qualified Stock Options (</i>&#8220;<i>NSOs</i>&#8221;<i>)</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">During the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025,&#160;</em>the Company granted to certain employees options to purchase&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142188683" contextRef="d_2025-02-01_2025-02-28_PlanNameAxis-The2022IncentiveAwardPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriodGross" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">686,647</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of Class A Common Stock at an exercise price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188684" contextRef="d_2025-02-01_2025-02-28_PlanNameAxis-The2022IncentiveAwardPlanMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementsByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriodWeightedAverageExercisePrice" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">11.07</ix:nonFraction>&#160;under the Company&#8217;s&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2022</em>&#160;Incentive Award Plan. During the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, </em>the Company granted to certain employees options to purchase <ix:nonFraction id="c142188686" contextRef="d_2024-02-01_2024-02-29_PlanNameAxis-The2022IncentiveAwardPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriodGross" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">438,781</ix:nonFraction> shares of Class A Common Stock at an exercise price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188687" contextRef="d_2024-02-01_2024-02-29_PlanNameAxis-The2022IncentiveAwardPlanMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementsByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriodWeightedAverageExercisePrice" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">11.63</ix:nonFraction> under the Company's <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Incentive Award Plan. The NSOs vest ratably over a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142188689">four</span>-year period beginning on the <em style="font: inherit;">sixth</em> anniversary of the grant date and have a term of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142188691">10</span> years.    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The realization of deferred tax assets, including net operating loss carryforwards ("NOLs"), is dependent on the generation of future taxable income sufficient to realize the tax deductions, carryforwards, and credits. Valuation allowances on deferred tax assets are recognized if it is determined that it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that the asset will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be realized. For the year&#160;ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, we recorded a full valuation allowance due to historical losses before income taxes which reduced management's ability to rely on future expectations of income.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>,&#160;we have available federal tax operating loss carryforwards of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188726" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-DomesticCountryMember_IncomeTaxAuthorityNameAxis-InternalRevenueServiceIRSMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">33.4</ix:nonFraction> million, including approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188727" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-DomesticCountryMember_IncomeTaxAuthorityNameAxis-InternalRevenueServiceIRSMember_LegalEntityAxis-YellowstoneAcquisitionCompanyMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million generated by our legal predecessor prior to the Yellowstone Transaction and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188728" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-DomesticCountryMember_IncomeTaxAuthorityNameAxis-InternalRevenueServiceIRSMember_LegalEntityAxis-StratusBuildingSystemMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">7.1</ix:nonFraction> million generated by our subsidiary, Stratus Building Systems. All federal tax operating loss carryforwards&#160;arose in tax years subsequent to <em style="font: inherit;">2017.</em>&#160;Tax operating loss carryovers arising in years after&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2017</em>&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>be carried forward indefinitely but are only available to offset <em style="font: inherit;">80%</em> of future taxable income. We have available state tax operating loss carryforwards of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188732" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-StateAndLocalJurisdictionMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">33.4</ix:nonFraction> million, which are available to reduce future state taxable income and would begin to expire in tax year <em style="font: inherit;">2040</em> in various amounts. Utilization of our net operating loss carryforwards <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be subject to substantial annual limitations due to the ownership change limitations provided by&#160;Section <em style="font: inherit;">382</em>&#160;of the Internal Revenue Code, as amended, and similar state provisions.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Uncertain Tax Positions</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">We believe that there are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> tax positions taken or expected to be taken that would significantly increase or decrease unrecognized tax benefits within <em style="font: inherit;">12</em> months of the reporting date.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The federal and state statutes of limitation for assessment of tax liability generally lapse within <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> years after the date the tax returns are filed. However, income tax attributes that are carried forward, such as net operating loss carryforwards, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be challenged and adjusted by taxing authorities at any time prior to the expiration of the statute of limitations for the tax year in which they are utilized. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have any open exams; however, all tax years, including those of our legal predecessor, are subject to examination by the Internal Revenue Service.&#160;&#160;</p>
