   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Tax Receivable Agreement</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">Following closing of the Yellowstone Transaction, the Company, Sky, the LLC Interests, and the TRA Holder Representative, entered into a tax receivable agreement (the &#8220;Tax Receivable Agreement&#8221;). Pursuant to the Tax Receivable Agreement, the Company will generally be required to pay the LLC Interests <em style="font: inherit;">85%</em> of the amount of savings, if any, in U.S. federal, state, local, and foreign taxes that are based on, or measured with respect to, net income or profits, and any interest related thereto that the Company realizes, or is deemed to realize, as a result of certain tax attributes, including:</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#8226; existing tax basis in certain assets of Sky and certain of its direct or indirect subsidiaries, including assets that will eventually be subject to depreciation or amortization, once placed in service, attributable to Sky Common Units acquired by the Company from a TRA Holder, as determined at the time of the relevant acquisition;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#8226; tax basis adjustments resulting from taxable exchanges of Sky Common Units (including any such adjustments resulting from certain payments made by the Company under the Tax Receivable Agreement) acquired by the Company from a TRA Holder pursuant to the terms of the A&amp;R Operating Agreement; and</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#8226; tax deductions in respect of portions of certain payments made under the Tax Receivable Agreement (each of the foregoing, collectively, the &#8220;Tax Attributes&#8221;).</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> transactions occurred that would result in a cash tax savings benefit that would trigger the recording of a liability under the terms of the Tax Receivable Agreement.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">Basic earnings (loss) per share of Class A Common Stock is computed by dividing net income (loss) attributable to SHG by the weighted-average number of shares of Class A Common Stock outstanding during the period. Diluted net income (loss) per share of Class A Common Stock is computed by dividing net income (loss) attributable to SHG, adjusted for the assumed exchange of all potentially dilutive securities, by the weighted-average number of shares of Class A Common Stock outstanding adjusted to give effect to potentially dilutive shares using the treasury stock or if-converted method as appropriate. Shares of the Company&#8217;s Class B Common Stock do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> participate in the earnings or losses of the Company and are therefore <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> participating securities. As such, separate presentation of basic and diluted earnings per share of Class B Common Stock under the <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>-class method has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been presented.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align:top;width:3.3%;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">19.</em> </b></p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:auto;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Segment Information</b></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The Company has&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142188756">one</span>&#160;consolidated reportable segment. This segment derives revenues from customers through the leasing of home-basing aircraft hangars and through services and products ancillary to its leasing activities. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>the Company drives revenue entirely within the United States&#160;and manages the business activities on a consolidated basis.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The determination of reportable operating segments is based on the Chief Operating Decision Maker&#8217;s (&#8220;CODM&#8217;s&#8221;) use of financial information provided for the purposes of assessing performance and making operating decisions. The Company's CODM is its founder and Chief Executive Officer. The CODM uses net income (loss) to allocate resources and assess the performance of the Company by comparing actual results to historical results and previously forecasted financial information and the allocation of budget between the expenses presented within the consolidated statement of operations. The measure of segment assets is reported on the consolidated balance sheet as total consolidated assets. All required significant financial segment information can be found within the consolidated financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The accounting policies of the Company&#8217;s consolidated segment are the same as those described in Note <em style="font: inherit;">2</em><i>&#160;</i>&#8212;&#160;<i>Basis of Presentation and Significant Accounting Policies.</i> Any intercompany revenues or expenses are eliminated in consolidation.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> December 6, 2024, </em>the Company entered into a revolving line of credit loan and security agreement&#160;(the &#8220;Loan and Security Agreement&#8221;), with a company controlled by the former owner of CloudNine and Sky <em style="font: inherit;">805,</em> who also serves as&#160;an independent contractor of the Company following the CMA Asset Acquisition. The Company provided an initial loan commitment of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188765" contextRef="i_2024-12-06_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-IndependentContractorMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LoansAndLeasesReceivableRelatedParties" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1.0</ix:nonFraction> million and agreed to provide an additional $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188766" contextRef="i_2024-12-06_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-IndependentContractorMember" unitRef="USD" name="skyh:LoansReceivableAdditionalWorkingCapitalLoanAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">2.0</ix:nonFraction> million of availability under a revolving line of credit to fund the working capital requirements of such company.    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Echo Echo Agreement</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> September 20, 2021, </em>the Company entered into a non-exclusive agreement with Echo Echo, LLC, a related party to the Founder and CEO, for the use of a Beechcraft Baron <em style="font: inherit;">G58</em> aircraft. The effective date of the agreement was <em style="font: inherit;"> September 8, 2021 </em>and the agreement automatically renews annually. The agreement could be terminated without penalty if either party provides <em style="font: inherit;">35</em> days'&#160;written notice, or if the aircraft is sold or otherwise disposed of. The Company was charged per flight hour of use along with all direct operating costs. Additionally, the Company also incurred the pro rata share of maintenance, overhead and insurance costs of the aircraft. On <em style="font: inherit;"> July 30, 2025, </em>the Company and Echo Echo, LLC terminated such agreement.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> September 19, 2024, </em>the Company entered into an additional non-exclusive agreement with Echo Echo, LLC for the use of an Epic <em style="font: inherit;">E1000GX</em> aircraft. The effective date of the agreement was <em style="font: inherit;"> August 30, 2024 </em>and the agreement automatically renews annually.&#160;The agreement can be terminated without penalty if either party provides <em style="font: inherit;">30</em> days' written notice, or if the aircraft is sold or otherwise disposed of. Additionally, the Company is responsible for reimbursing its&#160;pro rata share of the direct operating costs of the aircraft, exclusive of maintenance and insurance.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i>Tax-Exempt Warehouse Facility Amendments</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> January 8, 2026, </em>SH Capital II entered into an amendment (the &#8220;Amendment&#8221;) to the Credit Agreement.&#160;The Amendment amended the Credit Agreement to&#160;provide&#160;for, among other things, conditions under which surplus funds, as defined in the Amendment (the&#160;&#8220;Credit Agreement Surplus Funds&#8221;), <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be released to the Borrowers.&#160;Also on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 8, 2026, </em>subsidiaries of the Company that own hangar campuses at CMA and BDL were added to the borrowing base of the Credit Agreement. Subsequently, on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 8, 2026, </em>SH Capital II drew funds of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188787" contextRef="d_2026-01-08_2026-01-08_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfDebt" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">13</ix:nonFraction> million under the Credit Agreement in order to reimburse the Company for prior advances associated with capital expenditures at Bradley International Airport and certain other general corporate purposes. Following this draw, there was approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188788" contextRef="i_2026-01-08_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityRemainingBorrowingCapacity" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">187</ix:nonFraction> million in capacity under the Credit Agreement for future borrowings.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">In addition, SKYH III amended its related guaranty (the&#160;&#8220;Sky&#160;III Guaranty&#8221;), and such amendment, the &#8220;Sky III Guaranty Amendment&#8221;) to provide for, among other things, conditions under which surplus funds arising from&#160;amounts received by Sky from excess revenues released from the Master Indenture.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">Provided certain conditions within the Amendment are met, the Amendment permits the Borrowers to distribute or otherwise transfer such Credit Agreement Surplus Funds to (i) Sky (the &#8220;Parent Guarantor&#8221;) for the payment of general and administrative expenses of the Parent Guarantor, (ii) the payment of current interest or principal on indebtedness of the Parent Guarantor or indebtedness guaranteed by the Parent Guarantor, (iii) to deposit or transfer such funds into a separate account of an affiliate of the Parent Guarantor as security for the payment of principal&#160;of or interest on other&#160;indebtedness, or (iv) as a capital contribution of a Borrower&#160;for the approved construction and operation of hangar project facilities at various airports (the &#8220;Portfolio II&#160;Projects&#8221;, and such restriction on distributions and transfers the &#8220;Permissible Uses&#8221;). The Amendment&#160;permits the release of the Credit Agreement Surplus Funds beginning on the later&#160;of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2027 </em>or a trigger date based on substantial completion of certain Portfolio II Projects, and requires the Borrowers to maintain (i) a&#160;historical debt service coverage ratio, and a&#160;(ii) projected debt service coverage ratio, in each case determined on the last day of each fiscal quarter of the Borrowers, at a ratio of <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> less than <ix:nonFraction id="c142188790" contextRef="i_2027-01-01_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember_StatementScenarioAxis-ScenarioForecastMember" unitRef="Pure" name="skyh:DebtInstrumentCovenantProjectedDebtServiceCoverageRatio" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2.00</ix:nonFraction> to <em style="font: inherit;">1.00.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">The Sky III Guaranty Amendment permits the release of excess revenues released from the Master Trust on or after the later of (i) <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2027 </em>and (ii) <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> (<ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-08_2026-01-08_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" name="skyh:DebtInstrumentDurationTermAfterTheCapitalizedInterestEndDate" id="c142188793" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">3</ix:nonNumeric>) months after the Capitalized Interest End Date provided that (a) there are funds in excess of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188794" contextRef="i_2026-01-08_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-CreditAgreementMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="USD" name="skyh:DebtInstrumentReleaseOfExcessRevenueFundsOnDepositsInAccountsBenchmark" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">800,000</ix:nonFraction> on deposit in the accounts for such excess revenues on release date, and (b) to the extent there is a deficiency in any of the accounts under, there are sufficient funds on deposit (in addition to the minimum amount of funds held pursuant to cover such &#160;deficiency) and such funds are applied to remedy each such deficiency. The release of excess revenues is also subject to Permissible Uses.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">The above release conditions are also subject to the customary condition that there <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be any default under the Credit Agreement.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;"><i><em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Yorkville Promissory Note</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> January 27, 2026, </em>Sky issued a non-convertible, unsecured promissory note to Yorkville, in the aggregate principal amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188797" contextRef="i_2026-01-27_DebtInstrumentAxis-January2026YorkvillePromissoryNoteMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">10</ix:nonFraction> million (the <em style="font: inherit;"> &#8220;January 2026 </em>Yorkville Promissory Note&#8221;). The issue price for the <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2026 </em>Yorkville Promissory Note was <ix:nonFraction id="c142188798" contextRef="i_2026-01-27_DebtInstrumentAxis-January2026YorkvillePromissoryNoteMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="Pure" name="skyh:DebtInstrumentIssuancePricePercentageOfAggregatePrincipalAmount" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% of the aggregate principal amount thereof.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2026 </em>Yorkville Promissory Note accrues interest at a rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c142188799" contextRef="i_2026-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-January2026YorkvillePromissoryNoteMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">7.75</ix:nonFraction>% per annum (or <ix:nonFraction id="c142188800" contextRef="i_2026-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-January2026YorkvillePromissoryNoteMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="Pure" name="skyh:DebtInstrumentDefaultInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">18</ix:nonFraction>% upon the occurrence of an event of default) and matures on <em style="font: inherit;"> June 8, 2027. </em>Beginning on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 8, 2026, </em>and continuing on the same day of each of the <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em> successive months thereafter, Sky shall repay a portion of the outstanding balance of the <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2026 </em>Yorkville Promissory Note in an amount equal to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188802" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-January2026YorkvillePromissoryNoteMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentPeriodicPayment" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">833,333.33</ix:nonFraction>. The obligations of Sky&#160;under the <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2026 </em>Yorkville Promissory Note are guaranteed by the Company pursuant to a separate guaranty agreement between the Company and Yorkville. In connection with and pursuant to the <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2026 </em>Yorkville Promissory Note, the Company agreed to issue <ix:nonFraction id="c142188803" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-January2026YorkvillePromissoryNoteMember_StatementClassOfStockAxis-CommonClassAMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-RegisteredDirectOfferingMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">40,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of Class A Common Stock&#160;to Yorkville in a registered direct offering.    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i>Tax-Exempt Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Bonds&#160;Issuance</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> February 12, 2026, </em>Sky Harbour Capital III LLC (&#8220;Sky Capital III&#8221;), an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, completed a $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188806" contextRef="d_2026-02-12_2026-02-12_DebtInstrumentAxis-Series2026BondsMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfDebt" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">150</ix:nonFraction> million financing through the issuance of Revenue Bonds (Sky Harbour Capital III LLC Aviation Facilities Project), Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> (the &#8220;Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Bonds&#8221;). The Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Bonds were issued by the Public Finance Authority of Wisconsin, a multi-jurisdictional conduit issuer (the &#8220;Issuer&#8221;), pursuant to a Trust Indenture, dated as of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2026 (</em>the &#8220;Indenture&#8221;) and effective as of <em style="font: inherit;"> February 12, 2026, </em>between the Issuer and UMB Bank, N.A., as trustee (the &#8220;Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Bond Trustee&#8221;). The proceeds of the Bonds were used to make a loan (the &#8220;Loan&#8221;) to Sky Capital III pursuant to a Loan Agreement, dated as of <em style="font: inherit;"> February 1, 2026 (</em>the &#8220;Loan Agreement&#8221;), between the Issuer and Sky Capital III, and assigned to the Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Bond Trustee. The Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Bonds were issued in a limited offering (the &#8220;Offering&#8221;) pursuant to a Limited Offering Memorandum dated <em style="font: inherit;"> January 29, 2026 (</em>the &#8220;Limited Offering Memorandum&#8221;) to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule <em style="font: inherit;">144A</em> under the Securities Act of <em style="font: inherit;">1933,</em> as amended (the &#8220;Securities Act&#8221;) or accredited investors within the meaning of Rule <em style="font: inherit;">501</em>(a) under the Securities Act. The borrowings under the Loan Agreement are guaranteed (the &#8220;Guarantee&#8221;) by Sky, and Sky Harbour Holdings IV LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Sky (the &#8220;Pledgor&#8221;). Pursuant to the Indenture, all of the Issuer&#8217;s right, title, and interest in the Loan Agreement (except for certain unassigned rights) were assigned to the Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Bond Trustee. The Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Bonds are secured by the Loan Agreement and the residual cash flows of certain of the Company&#8217;s projects, and payment of the Bonds is structurally subordinate to the Series <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Bonds and borrowings under the Term Loan Facility.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Bonds and borrowings under the Loan Agreement bear interest at a rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c142188820" contextRef="i_2026-02-12_DebtInstrumentAxis-Series2026BondsMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">6.00</ix:nonFraction>% per year, payable semi-annually in arrears on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1 </em>of each year, beginning on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2026. </em>The Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Bonds are subject to mandatory tender for purchase on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2031 (</em>the &#8220;Mandatory Tender Date&#8221;), and will mature on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2060, </em>unless earlier exchanged, redeemed or repurchased. On the Mandatory Tender Date, holders will be required to tender their Bonds for purchase at a price equal to <ix:nonFraction id="c142188822" contextRef="d_2026-02-12_2026-02-12_DebtInstrumentAxis-Series2026BondsMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentRedemptionPricePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% of the principal amount thereof plus accrued interest. Following such mandatory tender, the Bonds <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be remarketed at a new interest rate or otherwise refinanced. Accordingly, although the Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Bonds have a stated final maturity of <em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2060, </em>Sky Capital III will be required to refinance or remarket the Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Bonds on or prior to <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2031.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The principal amount of the Loan is $<ix:nonFraction id="c142188825" contextRef="i_2026-02-12_DebtInstrumentAxis-Series2026BondsMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">150</ix:nonFraction> million. The Company intends to use the proceeds from the Loan, together with other available funds, including draws from the Company&#8217;s Term Loan Facility, to (i) finance or refinance, directly or indirectly, all or a portion of the construction, equipping and/or improvement of all or a portion of certain aircraft storage facilities (collectively, the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2026</em> Projects&#8221;); (ii) fund a deposit to the debt service reserve fund for the Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Bonds; (iii) pay capitalized interest on the Loan through <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2029; </em>and (iv) pay the costs of issuance of the Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Bonds.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">The Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Bonds are subject to (a) optional redemption at the discretion of Sky Capital III at any time on or after <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2030 </em>at a redemption price equal to the principal amount plus a <em style="font: inherit;">1%</em> premium and accrued and unpaid interest to the redemption date, (b) mandatory redemption upon the occurrence of a determination of taxability of the Series <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Bonds, and (c) mandatory sinking fund redemption beginning in <em style="font: inherit;">2056.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt; text-align: justify;">Sky Capital III expects to meet its payment obligations under the Loan Agreement from funds to the extent available and permitted to be released under the master trust indenture with respect to the Series <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Bonds and the Term Loan Facility. Interest is capitalized through <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2029.</em></p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b>Disclosure Controls and Procedures</b><br/> &#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">Disclosure controls and procedures are controls and other procedures that are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in our reports filed or submitted under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC&#8217;s rules and forms. Disclosure controls and procedures include, without limitation, controls and procedures designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in company reports filed or submitted under the Exchange Act is accumulated and communicated to management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">Pursuant to Rules 13a-15 and 15d-15 under the Exchange Act, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer (our principal executive officer and principal financial officer, respectively), with the participation of other members of management,&#160;carried out an evaluation of the effectiveness of the design and operation of our disclosure controls and procedures as of December 31, 2025. Our management does not expect that our disclosure controls and procedures will prevent or detect all errors and all fraud. Disclosure controls and procedures, no matter how well designed, operated and managed, can provide only reasonable assurance that the objectives of the disclosure controls and procedures are met. Because of the inherent limitations of disclosure controls and procedures, no evaluation of such disclosure controls and procedures can provide absolute assurance that all control issues and instances of fraud, if any, have been detected. Based upon this evaluation of our disclosure controls and procedures, our Chief Executive Officer and our Chief Financial Officer&#160;determined that our disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;<br/> <b>Management</b>&#8217;<b>s Report on Internal Controls over Financial Reporting</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company&#8217;s management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, as such term is defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) of the Exchange Act. The Company&#8217;s internal control system is designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with GAAP. Due to its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Therefore, even those systems determined to be effective can provide only reasonable assurance with respect to financial statement preparation and presentation.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">Management conducted an assessment of our internal control over financial reporting, including the remediation efforts described above,&#160;based upon criteria established in <i>Internal Control</i>&#8212;<i>Integrated Framework</i> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013). Based on that assessment, management determined that our internal controls over financial reporting were effective as of December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">There have not been any changes in our internal control over financial reporting, as such term is defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Exchange Act, during the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2025 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</p>

Schmitt and each of them, as his true and lawful attorney-in-fact and agent with full power of substitution, for him in any and all capacities, to sign any and all amendments to this Annual Report on Form 10-K, and to file the same, with all exhibits thereto and other documents in connection therewith, with the Securities and Exchange Commission, granting unto said attorney-in-fact and agent the full power and authority to do and perform each and every act and thing requisite and necessary to be done in connection therewith, as fully for all intents and purposes as he might or could do in person, hereby ratifying and confirming all that said attorney-in-fact and agent, or his substitute, may lawfully do or cause to be done by virtue thereof.</p>
